questions.question: What's the difference between render and redirect in Rails?
questions.title: Render vs Redirect
questions.direct_answer: render builds a response from the current request: render :show (a view), render json: @post (JSON), render plain: 'ok' — same request, you compose the body. redirect_to starts a NEW request: redirect_to @post tells the browser to GET /posts/:id (a 302), so the URL changes and the action re-runs. Rule of thumb: after a successful create/update/destroy, redirect (POST/redirect/GET pattern — avoids resubmitting on refresh); when you just need to show something, render. render re-renders the current view (e.g. form with errors on validation fail: render :new, status: :unprocessable_entity). One request vs two: render is one; redirect is two (the redirect + the new GET).

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know render composes the current response (one request) and redirect starts a new one (two requests), and the POST/redirect/GET rule.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: rendering after a create (refresh resubmits the form), or redirecting to re-render a form with validation errors (you lose the @post and the errors).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: render composes the current response (one request); redirect_to starts a new request (two). After create/update/destroy, redirect (POST/redirect/GET); render to show a form with errors.

sections.title: One Request vs Two
sections.content: render builds a response from the current request: render show (a view), render json at post (JSON), render plain ok — same request, you compose the body. redirect_to starts a NEW request: redirect_to post tells the browser to GET slash posts slash id (a 302), so the URL changes and the action re-runs. Rule of thumb: after a successful create, update, or destroy, redirect — the POST redirect GET pattern avoids resubmitting on refresh; when you just need to show something, render. render re-renders the current view — for example a form with errors on validation fail: render new, status unprocessable_entity. One request versus two: render is one; redirect is two, the redirect plus the new GET.

sections.title: render vs redirect_to
sections.content:
render = one request (compose the body); redirect = two (a 302, then a new GET).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  R[render :show] --> One[1 request: compose body]
  Rd[redirect_to @post] --> Two[2 requests: 302 + GET /posts/:id]
```

sections.title: render vs redirect
sections.content:
```ruby
# render: compose the current response (ONE request)
def show
  @post = Post.find(params[:id])
  render :show            # app/views/posts/show.html.erb
  # render json: @post    # JSON
  # render plain: 'ok'    # plain text
end

# redirect_to: start a NEW request (TWO requests: 302 + new GET)
def create
  @post = Post.create!(post_params)
  redirect_to @post       # browser GETs /posts/:id (URL changes)
  # POST/redirect/GET: refresh won't resubmit the form
end

# render to re-show a form with validation errors (same request)
def create
  @post = Post.new(post_params)
  if @post.save
    redirect_to @post
  else
    render :new, status: :unprocessable_entity  # 422, @post has errors
    # NOT redirect_to new_post_path (you'd lose @post + errors)
  end
end
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Rendering after a create — refresh resubmits the form (use redirect).
Redirecting to re-render a form with errors — you lose @post and the errors (render).
Forgetting status: :unprocessable_entity on render :new (Rails 7 needs it).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: render composes the current response (one request).
redirect_to starts a new request (two: the 302 + a new GET).
After create/update/destroy, redirect (POST/redirect/GET — avoids resubmitting on refresh).
To re-show a form with validation errors, render :new (keeps @post + errors), not redirect.
render :new on validation fail needs status: :unprocessable_entity in Rails 7.

sections.title: Spoken Answer
sections.content: render builds a response from the current request: render show (a view), render json at post (JSON), render plain ok — same request, you compose the body. redirect_to starts a NEW request: redirect_to post tells the browser to GET slash posts slash id (a 302), so the URL changes and the action re-runs. Rule of thumb: after a successful create, update, or destroy, redirect — the POST redirect GET pattern avoids resubmitting on refresh; when you just need to show something, render. render re-renders the current view — for example a form with errors on validation fail: render new, status unprocessable_entity. One request versus two: render is one; redirect is two, the redirect plus the new GET. A common mistake is rendering after a create, because refresh resubmits the form, and redirecting to re-render a form with errors, which loses @post and the errors.
